mcqs.learning_point: Recognise perpendicular lines as intersecting lines forming right angles
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines perpendicular lines?

options.A: Two lines that intersect to form a right angle (90°)
options.B: Two lines that never meet, no matter how far extended
options.C: Two lines that intersect at any angle less than 90°

mcqs.answer: Two lines that intersect to form a right angle (90°)
mcqs.explanation: Perpendicular lines are lines that meet at a point and create a right angle of 90°. Option B describes parallel lines, C describes acute intersecting lines, and D repeats the definition of parallel lines.

mcqs.question: In the figure, line AB is drawn horizontally, line CD is drawn vertically, and line EF is drawn at a 45° angle. Which pair of lines are perpendicular?
mcqs.explanation: A horizontal line and a vertical line meet at a right angle, so AB and CD are perpendicular. The other pairs form angles of 45° or are the same line, not right angles.

mcqs.learning_point: Use geometric reasoning to compare line relationships
mcqs.question: If line l1 is parallel to line l2, and line l2 is perpendicular to line l3, what is the relationship between l1 and l3?

options.C: l1 and l3 intersect at an acute angle
options.D: No definite relationship can be deduced

mcqs.explanation: When a line is parallel to another line, it inherits all angular relationships of that line. Since l2 is perpendicular to l3, any line parallel to l2 (i.e., l1) must also be perpendicular to l3. Hence l1 ⟂ l3.

mcqs.question: On a map, Road X runs north‑south, Road Y runs east‑west, and Road Z runs northeast‑southwest. Which two roads intersect each other?
mcqs.explanation: Road X (north‑south) and Road Y (east‑west) cross each other at a right‑angle intersection. While Road Z may cross one of them depending on exact placement, the guaranteed intersecting pair given the description is X and Y.

mcqs.question: Which statement about the intersection of two lines is correct?

options.A: They intersect at exactly one point.
options.B: They intersect at infinitely many points.

mcqs.answer: They intersect at exactly one point.
mcqs.explanation: Two distinct non‑parallel lines in a plane meet at a single, unique point. Parallel lines never meet (option C), coincident lines would intersect at infinitely many points (option B), and two points of intersection are impossible for straight lines (option D).

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise perpendicular lines as intersecting lines forming right angles
mcqs.question: If two lines are perpendicular, what can be said about the angle formed at their intersection?
mcqs.explanation: By definition, perpendicular lines intersect to create a right angle of 90°. Therefore option A is correct; the other options describe angles that are not right angles.

mcqs.question:
Four diagrams are described below. Which diagram shows a pair of perpendicular lines?
A) Two lines intersect forming a 45° angle.
B) One line is horizontal and another is vertical, intersecting.
C) Two lines are parallel and never meet.
D) Two lines intersect forming a 120° angle.
mcqs.explanation: A horizontal line and a vertical line meet at a right angle, which is the definition of perpendicular lines. Diagram A gives a 45° angle, Diagram C shows parallel lines, and Diagram D gives a 120° angle, none of which are perpendicular.

mcqs.learning_point: Use geometric reasoning to compare line relationships
mcqs.question: In triangle ABC, the altitude drawn from vertex A to side BC also bisects BC. Which type of triangle must ABC be?
mcqs.explanation: When an altitude from a vertex also serves as a median, the two sides adjacent to that vertex are equal, making the triangle isosceles. An equilateral triangle also satisfies this but is a special case; the statement guarantees at least an isosceles triangle. Options C and D do not necessarily satisfy both conditions.
